header:
Date: 2025-06-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Acme CTO), Maya Rivera (Acme ML Eng), Sonia Patel (Acme Security), Alex Gomez (Acme PM)
summary: POC scoping focused on success criteria signoff and acceptance tests for Acme's LLM-powered assistant. Agreed acceptance thresholds (latency, throughput, quality), dataset and benchmark plan, roles, and timeline. Action items assigned for benchmark artifacts, security docs, and scheduling the live run.
topics: Deployment options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood. We've got about 45 minutes, the goal is to lock down success criteria and acceptance tests for the POC. Priya, I'll let you cover the benchmark plan after quick intros.

[00:18] Priya Shah: yep hi all, Priya SE here. quick outline: we want to run two benchmark buckets - latency/throughput on your traces, and a small quality eval using your sample prompts. we'll provide an automated script you can run or we can run it from our side with a test account.

[00:35] Daniel Park: thanks. main ask from us is predictable p50/p95 latency and a cost envelope. also we need to see no data leaves our VPC for the Private option, and audit logs for any Dedicated runs.

[00:50] Maya Rivera: and from model quality side, we have three top level use cases - customer support summarization, internal search reranking and code generation snippets. we care about F1-ish metrics for rerank and ROUGE for summarization but mostly subjective evals too.

[01:10] Sonia Patel: quick security note - we require SOC2 plus our vendor DPA, KMS integration for key management, and SSO with SAML for any console access. we'll need to review your SOC2 report and pen test summary.

[01:30] Alex Gomez: timeline: we want pilot signed by end of month if possible. so benchmark run next week, then go/no-go decision within 72 hours of results.

[01:45] Priya Shah: ok, acceptance tests we propose: 1) Latency: p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 400ms for 90% of traffic pattern; 2) Throughput: sustain 200 req/s with <=5% tail degradation; 3) Quality: automated eval thresholds - e.g. rerank NDCG@10 delta <= 2% vs baseline and human eval score >= 4/5 on 50 sampled prompts; 4) Stability: no memory leaks or KV cache thrash across 24h run; 5) Security: KMS-managed keys, SOC2 evidence, and audit logs available. Are those OK?

[02:20] Daniel Park: p50 200ms is ambitious but sounds reasonable for hosted. for Dedicated we'd expect better; we need to see both numbers. the throughput target is fine. can you define "sustain" — do you mean steady-state or burst?

[02:35] Priya Shah: good point. sustain == steady-state for 30 minutes with the same concurrency profile as your trace. we'll run both a steady-state 30min and a 5min burst to capture tail behavior.

[02:50] Maya Rivera: on quality thresholds, the rerank baseline is our current in-house model, not SOTA. we can provide the labeled set. also for summarization we'll run ROUGE-L and a small human blind eval of 50 examples.

[03:05] Jordan Lee: noted. reporting format: we'll produce a PDF summary + CSVs with per-request latencies, token counts, model used, and a short slide deck with findings. would you prefer a dashboard link instead?

[03:20] Alex Gomez: CSV + slides please, dashboard optional. we want the raw per-request logs for our own analysis.

[03:35] Sonia Patel: on KMS, we need details of how you handle envelope encryption, key rotation, and whether Redwood stores any plaintext keys. also ID the data residency if crossing regions.

[03:50] Priya Shah: we support customer-managed KMS in both Dedicated and Private. for Hosted Api we can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping on request in some cases — i'll send the exact spec. we do not persist plaintext keys; envelope keys are used and rotated based on policy.

[04:10] Daniel Park: good. cost question: can you give a rough estimate for the Dedicated run required to hit 200 req/s for our model family?

[04:20] Priya Shah: rough estimate: for a 1B-ish decoder model with quantization and batching tuned you should see 200 req/s on 4xA100-equivalent in Dedicated with optimizations. cost estimate i'll put in the follow-up but expected ballpark commit for pilot about $Xk/month — we'll provide a clearer number when we see your token distribution.

[04:45] Maya Rivera: another operational ask: can you support prefix/KV caching for chat-style prompts? our support use case relies heavily on long context reuse.

[04:55] Priya Shah: yes, our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching, and we can configure cache TTL and shard policies for your workload. we'll include cache hit rate in the benchmark report.

[05:10] Jordan Lee: ok let's capture the final success criteria on this call so we can sign off. I'll read them back: Latency p50 <=200ms p95 <=400ms on Hosted baseline, Dedicated numbers to be measured and expected better; Throughput sustain 200 req/s steady-state 30m; Quality: NDCG delta <=2% and human eval >=4/5 on 50 samples; Stability no memory leaks across 24h; Security: SOC2 report, KMS integration, SSO. Go/no-go: results shared, 72 hours for decision window. Any objections?

[05:45] Daniel Park: no objections. sounds good. we want the benchmark script and the sample labeled set by Wednesday.

[05:55] Alex Gomez: also please flag any model quantization changes that may affect quality so we can review.

[06:05] Priya Shah: will do. also note we'll run both Hosted API and Dedicated variants and include cost per 1M tokens in the report.

[06:20] Maya Rivera: on the human eval, can Redwood manage blind annotation and scoring or do you want us to do it?

[06:30] Jordan Lee: we can run the blind annotation for you and provide the scoring sheet; if you'd rather run it internally we can provide the format.

[06:40] Sonia Patel: final security note: please attach your pen test summary and list of sub-processors in the follow-up email.

[06:50] Jordan Lee: absolutely. quick recap of next steps: (1) Jordan/Priya share benchmark script + instructions and link to repo; (2) Acme shares 24h trace + labeled set; (3) Redwood schedules benchmark run and shares raw CSVs + slide deck; (4) Security docs and cost estimate shared. target run on 2025-06-10 and follow-up 2025-06-12.

[07:10] Daniel Park: thanks everyone. sounds like we're aligned.

[07:18] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD with the artifacts. bye.

Notes: transcription contains small mis-hearings (e.g., Redwood product names sometimes transcribed as Red wood, KV cache as K-V cash etc.), occasional speaker mislabels in automated export. Links: benchmark script repo (private) https://redwood.ai/internal/acme-poc-benchmarks (access granted to attendees), security docs link https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (for reference).
